title: Delay self-application with Z
description: You can compare two fixed-point combinators under Python's call-by-value evaluation.

steps.description: Y evaluates x(x) as an argument. Z wraps that self-application in another lambda, delaying it until a call supplies v.
fact_gen receives its recursive operation as self. Z supplies that operation, and the displayed calls return 1 and 120.
fib_gen uses the same supplied self twice in its recursive branch.

steps.question: Does the Y example reach a factorial call before it fails?
steps.answer: No. Evaluating Y(fact_gen) already repeats self-application until RecursionError.

steps.description: The exception handler identifies failure during construction. The expected-output comments contrast that failure with the delayed recursion through Z.
